To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The production cross section of W − W − ( W + W + ) pairs in collisions of equally charged muons (electrons), induced by Majorana neutrino flavor, is large and rises with center of mass energy; (ii) the cross section is large even for small neutrino mixing; (iii) the signal is clean, with no background; (iv) the signal is unique, and constitutes a clear discovery channel for Tev level Majorana neutrinos
the production rate of W W pairs in the collisions of two equally-charged leptons is enhanced by the exchange of heavy Majorana neutrinos and is a discovery channel for the heavy neutrinos.

the cross section σ ( l l → W W ) for the process l l → W + W + / W − W −, mediated by a heavy neutrino, is large enough to be detected at the LHC and at future linear colliders; that this process is the most promising discovery channel for Tev-level Majorana neutrino flavors, and that the cross section is a sensitive function of the heavy neutrino’s mass and mixing parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Can the existence of a heavy neutrino flavor be experimentally verified in the near future?
the search for heavy neutrinos with masses of the order of a few TeV, and mixing with the light neutrinos.
the search for heavy neutrinos and the discovery of lepton flavor violating processes.

the heavy neutrino discovery potential of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is far from being exhausted by the current experimental program.
